lede: The biggest thing to watch this week is Tuesday's Town Council session, where work sessions cover the Comprehensive Plan, a Gondola Subcommittee update, and — most consequentially — a review of proposals for a third-party audit of the Town's rental housing policies, which goes to the heart of who can actually afford to live here. Ouray County's Planning Commission also meets virtually Wednesday to work through possible Land Use Code definition changes, the kind of quiet groundwork that shapes what gets built and where. Mountain Village's Design Review Board takes up a conditional-use permit for a temporary tent and food truck on Adams Ranch Road Thursday.

notable.stake: Third-party audit of rental housing policies could reshape who stays in Telluride.
Land Use Code definition changes are being shaped before any public hearing.
Conditional-use permit for Adams Ranch Rd tent and food truck goes to DRB for recommendation.
